turns.text: Hey Lloyd, I'm looking at specs for that new EPYC 9004 series server. The whitepaper says the optimal core count for our inference workloads is 32 cores.
Got it. 32 cores is a solid baseline for high-throughput tasks. Did you check the TDP on those chips?
Yeah, 200W. A bit high. Also, did my package for the NVMe drive arrive?
Tracking shows it was delivered yesterday. Check your front porch.
Found it. Thanks. Back to the server, 32 cores seems to be the sweet spot they recommend.
Understood. I've noted that 32 cores is the recommended target for your current setup.
Lloyd, I re-ran the benchmarks on the CPU Inference cluster. It turns out the old advice was wrong. Beyond 8-16 cores, additional cores provide diminishing returns as memory bandwidth saturates.
That’s a significant shift. So 32 cores is actually over-provisioned for most of our standard workloads?
Exactly. We’re seeing thermal throttling and no throughput gain past 16. I'm thinking of downgrading the next batch of nodes.
Makes sense. Memory bandwidth is often the bottleneck before compute cores run out.
Yeah. Also, is it going to rain this weekend? I wanted to wash the car.
Looks like clear skies on Saturday, but rain is likely by Sunday afternoon.
Perfect, I'll wash it Saturday. Anyway, stick with the 8-16 core rule for the config templates.
Updated. I will use the 8-16 core range for future recommendations.
